## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rūpāvacarakusala* (Ds 2.1.2) constitutes the major division of the Dhammasaṅgaṇī dedicated to wholesome phenomena (*kusalā dhammā*) belonging to the fine-material sphere (*rūpāvacara*) [Gethin 2001; Frauwallner 1995]. Within the *cittuppādakaṇḍa*, the Dhammasaṅgaṇī divides wholesome consciousness across four planes: sense-sphere (*kāmāvacara*), fine-material (*rūpāvacara*), immaterial (*arūpāvacara*), and supermundane (*lokuttara*) [Gethin 2001]. In this section, meditative absorption is expounded systematically across both the fourfold and fivefold schemes of *jhāna*, integrating traditional canonical meditation sets such as the *kasiṇa* devices, the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhāyatana*), the liberations (*vimokkha*), and the meditations on the unattractive (*asubha*) [Frauwallner 1995]. SuttaCentral catalogs this text as a leaf section and records two modern translations [SuttaCentral].

DharmaNexus identifies extensive formulaic reuse across the Pali Abhidhamma, registering 17,389 matches across 124 texts [DharmaNexus]. Internally, it shares its greatest textual volume with the *Lokuttarakusala* (Ds 2.1.5) and *Kāmāvacarakusala* (Ds 2.1.1) sections of the Dhammasaṅgaṇī, followed by Vibhaṅga treatises including the *Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga* (Vb 15), *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), and *Jhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 12) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns this material cross-linguistically with Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese treatises detailing canonical *jhāna* and *dhyāna* classifications, including the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, and the Chinese *Dīrghāgama* [DharmaNexus].
